# Incident Report — 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F (NetBIOS alias WIRESHARKWORKSH) |
| Logged-in Windows user | ccollier |
| OS (from malware beacon) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |
| Domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (AD domain controller WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) |

Identity grounded in NBNS name registrations from 172.16.1.66 (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F`, `WIRESHARKWORKSH`), Kerberos `CNameString` fields (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`), and ARP (172.16.1.66 ↔ 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08).

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** — a Java-based remote access trojan.

**Attribution confidence: signature-confirmed.** The malware's own C2 protocol identifies itself by name in plaintext on the wire. TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132) contains repeating pipe-delimited beacons of the form:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

This is STRRAT's documented "ping" heartbeat format (version tag `1.6`), sent every ~5 seconds, unencrypted, on a non-standard port with no TLS handshake — consistent with STRRAT's known cleartext socket C2. The capture does not contain the initial infection/delivery artifact (dropper, jar, or email), so only the active-infection/C2 phase is confirmed; the delivery vector is outside the scope of this pcap.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — TCP, cleartext STRRAT beacon protocol. Evidence: tcp.stream 83, first SYN at frame 9066 (t=76.99s), beaconing continuously through the end of the capture (last frame 11562, t=585.66s). No corresponding DNS lookup for this IP was observed — it was contacted directly by hardcoded IP.

**Bot/campaign identifier**
- `1BE8292C` — STRRAT bot ID embedded in every beacon (evidence: tcp.stream 83 payload).

**Supporting/attacker-facing lookup**
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) — HTTP GET `/json/` from 172.16.1.66 at frame 9111, response includes geolocation (`"countryCode":"US","region":"TX","city":"Austin"`). This immediately precedes the STRRAT beacon reporting `US:United States`, indicating the malware queried ip-api.com to populate its own geolocation field before/during C2 beaconing. Not malicious infrastructure by itself, but functionally tied to the STRRAT beacon content — flagged as a supporting IOC rather than a C2 endpoint.

**Malicious domains/URLs**
- None observed. The C2 channel used a bare IP:port (141.98.10.79:12132) with no DNS resolution and no HTTP/TLS SNI, so there is no domain or URL to report for the C2 channel itself.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- None observed. No executable, JAR, or other payload transfer appears in this capture (`--export-objects http` yielded only benign Microsoft/Windows telemetry, `connecttest.txt`, and the `ip-api.com` JSON response — no jar/exe/PE content). The malware was already resident and beaconing when the capture begins; delivery is not captured.

## Benign Context (ruled out, not IOCs)
The remaining high-volume traffic is legitimate Windows/Microsoft ecosystem and domain-joined activity: Kerberos/LDAP/CLDAP/DRSUAPI/SMB to the domain controller 172.16.1.4; TLS to Microsoft telemetry, MSN, Bing, Skype, Office, WNS, and Windows Update endpoints (13.107.x, 20.189.x, 23.x Akamai, 40.126.x, 52.109.x, 204.79.197.203); GitHub (140.82.113.3, `objects.githubusercontent.com` 185.199.110.133); Maven Central (`repo1.maven.org`, 199.232.196.209 — largest single conversation by byte volume, 8.9 MB, consistent with a legitimate Java/Maven build or dependency fetch on this workstation, plausibly related to the host having a Java runtime present that STRRAT itself abuses); Oracle Java update check (`javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`); and SSDP/mDNS/NBNS/LLMNR local-segment discovery noise.

## Incident Summary
The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user `ccollier` on the `wiresharkworkshop.online` domain, is compromised with the **STRRAT** Java-based RAT (bot ID `1BE8292C`). Starting at t=76.99s in the capture, the infected host establishes a persistent, unencrypted TCP session to **141.98.10.79:12132** and sends heartbeat "ping" messages roughly every 5 seconds for the remainder of the capture, self-identifying as STRRAT and reporting host/user/OS details plus a geolocation string sourced from a preceding `ip-api.com` lookup. No payload delivery or additional attacker-issued commands were captured in this window; only the standing C2 heartbeat is present.
